title: WorkloadContract v1alpha1
description: The declarative interface an application team uses to describe one InferOps workload. This schema is structural only: cross-field rules that JSON Schema cannot express are stated in docs/contracts/workload-contract.md and are not enforced here.

apiVersion.description: Contract group and maturity version. A breaking change requires a new value here, never a redefinition of this one.

dnsLabel.description: A DNS-safe stable identifier, lowercase, as required for workload, owner, tenant, and capability identity.

digestPinnedImageReference.description: An OCI image reference pinned by digest. A tag alone is a movable label and is not accepted.

repositoryPath.description: A path relative to the repository root. Absolute paths, parent traversal, and drive letters are rejected so that a contract cannot carry a personal filesystem path.

kubernetesQuantity.description: A resource quantity in documented Kubernetes units, for example 500m, 2, 2Gi, or 1500Mi.

name.description: workload_id. Stable, DNS-safe, and unique within an environment.

version.description: workload_version. An immutable release identity: a semantic version or an image reference pinned by digest.

owner.description: owner_id. The owning team's stable platform catalogue identifier. A workload without an owner has nobody to page.

annotations.description: The single extension point of this contract. Keys are namespaced to a DNS domain the annotator controls. Values are non-normative: the platform must not change behaviour because of one.

profile.description: The workload profile. mock-llm exists for deterministic contract tests in continuous integration and can never certify real serving.

environment.description: Deployment environment, from a controlled vocabulary.

proofRefs.description: A mock workload has no real-runtime proof, so it may not cite any. This is the schema-level half of the mock and real serving boundary.

model.description: The common model and runtime reference. Anything specific to one profile lives in that profile's own block, never here.

servingCapability.description: capability_id of the serving capability this workload binds to.

modelRef.description: The registered model identity within the platform catalogue. The bytes behind it are pinned in the profile block, not here.

runtimeProfile.description: The runtime sizing intent. It expresses what the workload is asking for, not what any host was measured to deliver.

resources.description: Explicit resource declaration. There is no default: an unsized workload is rejected rather than guessed at.

integrations.description: Declared platform dependencies. Telemetry is not optional: a workload the platform cannot observe cannot be operated.

required.description: true when the workload cannot perform its declared function without this capability.

secretRefs.description: References to secrets, never secret values. Every member object is closed, so there is no field a value could be written into.

name.description: The logical name the workload uses to consume this secret.

reference.description: A locator for the secret. Whitespace, quotes, and assignment characters are excluded so that the shapes a pasted value usually takes cannot be written here. This is a constraint, not a proof: see the contract document for what it does not catch.

owner.description: owner_id of the team responsible for this secret's contents.

rotation.description: Who is responsible for rotating it. Unstated rotation responsibility is how a credential outlives the person who created it.

tenant.description: tenant_id. Declared here, but validated or injected by a trusted platform component rather than trusted from this document.

runbookRef.description: Repository-relative path to the operational procedure for this workload.

proofRefs.description: Repository-relative paths to executed-proof records supporting this workload's claims.

synchronousLlm.description: Fields specific to the synchronous-llm profile. Present only for that profile.

modelArtifact.description: The exact bytes to be served, pinned by upstream revision and by content hash. Either alone is insufficient: a revision names what was published, a hash names what arrived.

mockLlm.description: Fields specific to the mock-llm profile. Present only for that profile, and self-labelling so that a reader who sees only this block still knows what it is.

ciOnly.description: Always true. Written into the artifact rather than inferred from the directory it sits in, so that the label survives being copied.

determinism.description: How the mock produces responses. Only fixed fixtures are permitted, because a mock that varies is a mock nobody can assert against.

fixtureRef.description: Repository-relative path to the deterministic response fixture this mock replays.
